sam: quick heads up — ran 8xA100 pipelined inference (tp=2 pp=2) with LL128 on and saw intermittent tail spikes during large-batch traffic. hypothesis: channel scheduling + algo/proto selection is starving small collectives. sharing traces.

anya: can you drop the perf trace / nvprof snippet?

sam: pasted raw trace (trimmed):
```
[trace] 0.02s gpu0 allreduce size=64B channel=3 wait=0.88ms
[trace] 0.03s gpu1 allreduce size=64B channel=7 wait=12.4ms
[trace] 0.10s gpu0 large-kernel exec 4.5ms
[trace] gpu1 queue len: 18
```
```
NCCL_PROTO=LL
NCCL_ALGO=Ring
NCCL_LL128_ENABLE=1
NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS
export NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=GPU
```

cheung: interesting — channel 7 seems heavily loaded. do we have per-channel fifo / priority? current runtime uses simple round-robin mapping so large kernels can occupy channels and starve small allreduces.

ryan: what if we add a lightweight priority queueing for collectives: small allreduces get preemptive slots on at least one channel and we demote large kernels to different set? similar to packet QoS but per-channel.

nate: would that interact badly with kernel selection? some kernels prefer LL128 path for bandwidth; preempting them might cause more kernel-switch overhead.

sam: did a quick experiment: enabled "collective_priority=1" local patch that pins small allreduces to channels [0,1] and demotes large convs to [2..7]. results on same trace: throughput +11%, p99 latency -28% for short reduces. no obvious correctness issues.

anya: nice — can you share the command used to run the experiment so infra can reproduce?

sam: repro:
```
./run_infer --model xlarge --tp 2 --pp 2 --batch 1024 --nccl-env 'NCCL_PROTO=LL;NCCL_LL128_ENABLE=1' --collective-priority=1
```

infra-bot: perf job queued (job id 2087654321-repro). cc @perf-bot

perf-bot: perf job finished: baseline(LL128 default) -> repro(collective_priority=1): tokens/sec +12%, p99 latency -26%, allreduce wait mean -9ms. raw traces uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/2087654321/

cheung: great. follow-ups: (1) add per-channel queue len metrics to Console, (2) add a kernel selection signal to avoid demoting kernels where LL128 yields >1.15x bandwidth, (3) run with different algo/proto combos (LL vs SIMPLE) to ensure heuristics stable.

ryan: also test with kvcache cold-warm transitions — if kvcache eviction causes transient kernels, priority could oscillate. add a small hysteresis.

nate: noted — I'll open a PR with a prototype + toggles and a small perf harness for per-channel stress test.

sam: thanks — filing a follow-up ticket: PLATFORM-6178 (collective-priority heuristic + console metrics). @anya can you assign to nate/ryan/cheung? :thumbsup:

anya: assigned. i'll add perf run matrix (LL/LL128, RING/Tree, collective_priority 0/1) and schedule on next perf cluster window.

sam: awesome. closing for now, we'll reconvene after perf matrix completes. :rocket:
